item.title: Best Practices for Using HPC: Scaling Up to Cluster-Native Workflows
item.description:
Moving Beyond the Laptop Mindset: A Practical Guide for Researchers and Computational Scientists

Abstract

Unlocking the full potential of advanced computational infrastructure requires moving beyond the mindset of simply scaling up local code. While transitioning from a personal workstation or Google Colab notebook to a shared High-Performance Computing (HPC) cluster removes local compute and memory bottlenecks, true acceleration is achieved only by adopting cluster-native workflows.

Modern supercomputing systems are not simply bigger laptops; they are orchestrated, multi-tenant community ecosystems governed by batch schedulers, distributed parallel filesystems, and specialized hardware accelerators. Navigating these environments demands an operational paradigm shift.

item.title: Vibe Coding for Scientists and Researchers
item.description:
Moving Science Forward with a New Way of Practice

Abstract

In empirical research, progress is frequently constrained not by the breadth of human scientific imagination, but by the friction of computational implementation. While the broader tech community has embraced “vibe coding” as a rapid prototyping methodology for consumer applications, this article formalizes vibe coding habits for scientists and researchers as a disciplined, hypothesis-driven workflow for computational scholars, graduate students, and faculty. By coupling declarative natural language intent with zero-trust synthetic benchmarking, invariant assertion, and automated provenance tracking, researchers can compress months of pipeline engineering into hours without compromising scientific reproducibility or mathematical validity.
